==============================================================================
SHOOTINGSTAR PHASE 0 -- IMPLIED COMPRESSION CEILING
==============================================================================
machine     : 33.4 GB/s read (4 threads), 1211 GOP/s int8
              machine balance 36.3 ops/byte
model       : llama-2-7b, 6.61B decode params @ 4-bit
atlas       : TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0 / held_out / 16384 tokens

BASELINE      3303.5 MB/token  ->    10.1 tok/s roofline ceiling
            arithmetic intensity 4.0 ops/byte vs balance 36.3
            => 89% of this machine's arithmetic is IDLE during decode

LEVERS (error budget: 5% of residual norm)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
lever                         bytes x  speedup   basis
mlp_contextual_sparsity         0.750     1.33x  exact truncation error <= 5% of residual norm; mean keep-fra
                                                requires a predictor for WHICH neurons, and a gather-matmul kern
                                                el; neither is priced in here
attn_head_sparsity              0.960     1.04x  exact truncation error <= 5% of residual norm; mean keep-fra
                                                counts q_proj+o_proj only; k/v are shared across a GQA group and
                                                 survive unless the whole group is dropped
layer_dropping                  1.000     1.00x  0/22 layers with cos(in,out) >= 0.95: []
                                                quality cost is measured independently in results/gate_selftest.
                                                json
speculative_decoding            0.809     1.24x  mean run of 0.41 consecutive tokens with top-1 prob > 0.8 (e [lossless]
                                                ORACLE UPPER BOUND: assumes the drafter guesses every 'easy' tok
                                                en. A real drafter is worse. Draft cost charged at 10%.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LOSSLESS ONLY                   0.809     1.24x  <- safe to bank
NAIVE PRODUCT (all)             0.582     1.72x

  bytes/token  3303.5 MB -> 1924.2 MB
  ceiling      10.1 -> 17.3 tok/s (DRAM bandwidth)

  measured baseline (llama.cpp): 5.50 tok/s
  10x target                   : 55.00 tok/s
  implied ceiling vs target    : SHORT (0.32x of target)

!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
CAVEAT. Each lever above is measured. Their PRODUCT is not.
Nothing here shows these compose: contextual sparsity may not survive
aggressive quantisation, and layer dropping and speculative decoding
may be eating the same redundancy (both exploit 'this token was easy').
Treat the product as an UPPER BOUND to be falsified in Phase 1.
Also unpriced: every lever needs a kernel that actually skips the
memory traffic. A technique with no kernel is a paper, not a speedup.
!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

levers.name: mlp_contextual_sparsity
levers.basis: exact truncation error <= 5% of residual norm; mean keep-fraction 0.62 of 5632 neurons
levers.note: requires a predictor for WHICH neurons, and a gather-matmul kernel; neither is priced in here

levers.name: attn_head_sparsity
levers.basis: exact truncation error <= 5% of residual norm; mean keep-fraction 0.75 of heads
levers.note: counts q_proj+o_proj only; k/v are shared across a GQA group and survive unless the whole group is dropped

levers.name: layer_dropping
levers.note: quality cost is measured independently in results/gate_selftest.json

levers.name: speculative_decoding
levers.basis: mean run of 0.41 consecutive tokens with top-1 prob > 0.8 (easy fraction 0.29)
levers.note: ORACLE UPPER BOUND: assumes the drafter guesses every 'easy' token. A real drafter is worse. Draft cost charged at 10%.
